title: Event recap
summary: An aftermovie or recap of an event the user filmed (conference, meetup, party, wedding, concert, offsite): many clips from several devices cut to music, a few soundbites, 30 s to 3 min, plus vertical cut-downs.

notFor.when: a montage from licensed stock or supplied b-roll that is not footage of an event the user held or attended
clips cut out of one long recording of a talk, a stream or a podcast
one speaker's recording to tidy, caption or reframe
a film announcing an event that has not happened yet

qa: No person who opted out, no child without a parent's consent and no private moment appears identifiably
Clips from different devices read as one grade: matched white balance, contrast and black level across every cut
Each soundbite is a whole thought, intelligible over the ducked music, captioned, with the speaker's name spelled as on the programme
Music from the venue or the performers is not left under the film's track unless its rights are cleared for every placement
Every vertical cut-down is re-edited from vertical-safe selects, not a centre crop of the master

intake.ask: Where are the clips, who shot them on which devices, and may every contributor's footage be published?
intake.why: Selects start from the full set; a guest's phone clip needs that guest's permission like any outside footage.

intake.ask: How were attendees told about filming (notice at the entrance, ticket terms, lanyards), and did anyone opt out or were children present?
intake.why: Decides which faces may appear: notice and legitimate interest at a large event, consent at a small one, a parent's consent for children.

intake.ask: Which names, numbers and moments must appear (programme, speakers, sponsors, attendance), with names spelled as published?
intake.why: The facts and the chronology come from the organiser, not from guessing at the footage.
intake.default: No names or numbers on screen beyond the event's name and date.

intake.ask: Where will it be published, and is the music to be one track licensed for every placement or each platform's own library?
intake.why: A track from TikTok's or Meta's library is licensed only on that platform; a Short over one minute with a music claim is blocked.
intake.default: One track from the sound-director's shortlist, licensed for every placement.

intake.ask: Who may be heard: which speakers, toasts or interviews are soundbites, and in which language?
intake.why: Soundbites need a clear recording and the speaker's agreement to be quoted; they set where the music ducks.
intake.default: No soundbites: music and the crowd's own sound only.

intake.ask: Which lengths and formats: the master and its cut-downs?
intake.why: A cut-down is re-edited from its own selects, so each one is planned, not cropped afterwards.
intake.default: A 60 s landscape master and a 30 s vertical cut-down.

profiles.note: Reels run to 3 min; under 90 s is a house rule. Business accounts keep to Meta's Sound Collection or a track licensed for Meta.
Businesses may not use the general music library: the Commercial Music Library or an own licensed track.
Shorts run to 3 min, but one over 1 min with an active Content ID claim is blocked worldwide: venue music counts.
Clean master with an SRT from the soundbites; the full aftermovie lives here.
Conference and offsite recaps; LinkedIn accepts 1:2.4 to 2.4:1 up to 15 min, the band is a house rule.
Event page or next year's sales page; house rule: the first 5 s read without sound, in case the player starts muted.

starter.note: Picture is the footage; library type only for the event's name, one number, each soundbite speaker's lower third and soundbite captions, inside one film-finish.

variants.title: Wedding film
variants.changes: A private event: the couple approves every guest shown and the soundbites (vows, toasts) carry the story; a 3-5 min film plus a 60 s teaser; music the couple chooses, licensed for where they post it.

variants.title: Conference or meetup recap
variants.changes: Speaker soundbites and the programme's names on screen; one or two numbers (attendees, talks); a filming notice usually covers the crowd, but speakers agree to be quoted; LinkedIn and the event site are the main placements.

variants.title: Concert or festival aftermovie
variants.changes: The performance is the music: its recording rights come from the artist and label, not the organiser; otherwise cut to a licensed track and keep live crowd sound under it. Energy builds to a peak late in the film.
